summary.headline: FirstCry Q4 FY26: consol revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr for FY26; Q4 adjusted EBITDA up 18% to ₹118.7 Cr amid India gross margin pressure.
summary.overview: Brainbees (FirstCry) reported Q4 and FY26 with consolidated FY26 revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr, adjusted EBITDA up 24% to about ₹486 Cr, and free cash flow positive for the full year. India multi-channel grew 11.4% in Q4 but gross margin fell on diaper price competition from quick-commerce and horizontal players, plus a transitory manufacturing hit from rupee depreciation and crude-linked inputs. Management says the offline channel grew about 15% in Q4 after a product-mix shift, and that RocketBees and Qwik delivery initiatives are lifting service levels, with the benefit expected to show in FY27. International losses fell 35% in FY26 and GlobalBees core categories grew 28%.

segments.name: India multi-channel
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +11.4% and FY26 revenue +9%; GMV +11% in FY26, crossing $1 billion for the first time. Management says the segment stayed PAT and cash flow positive in FY26. Non-diapering is over 85% of GMV; diapering (about 15% of business) faces heavy price competition.

segments.name: International (UAE and KSA)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue above $100 million, growing about 10% in FY26; Q4 revenue +9%. Gross margin rose 240 bps for FY26 (470 bps in Q4). Management did not give a timeline for reaching break-even.

segments.name: GlobalBees
segments.commentary: FY26 consolidated revenue +20% (organic, after brand rationalisation) and core categories +28%. Adjusted EBITDA post-corporate expenses was 5.8% of revenue in Q4 (₹26.5 Cr) and about 3% for FY26 after ESOP cost. Brand rationalisation is expected to finish by end Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Others (preschool)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue +11% with EBITDA margin about 27% (vs 24% in FY25). Preschools more than doubled from 208 at end FY24, and enrolled students are almost 3x in two years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 India multi-channel GMV and revenue growth guided to be much superior to FY26; management expects sequential quarterly improvement to continue.
India multi-channel FY27 EBITDA (rupee terms) guided to grow double digits, per management's 'should' answer; margin expansion expected outside diapering.
Gross margin loss from the Q3 diaper competition (about 140 bps) expected to take 4-6 quarters to reverse; manufacturing-related loss expected to be recovered from Q2 FY27 via pass-through.
Company-owned and FOFO stores: about 100 openings planned in FY27 after pausing COCO openings in FY26 (10 COCO stores added in FY26).
Qwik expected to reach roughly 10% of total B2C online shipments over FY27; RocketBees already at 40%+ of online delivery volume, with a target of 45-50% by mid-2026.
Continued international loss reduction in FY27; management aims to take losses to zero as early as possible.
capex_capacity: RocketBees own-network coverage grew from 13 cities (Q2) to 22 (Q3) to 62 cities (Q4); management aims to cross 50 cities by next quarter-end.
Qwik quick-delivery pilot began 1 Dec 2025 and now runs in 5 cities; it delivers in under 3 hours and is already over 20% of online orders in the covered catchments.
Logistics cost front-loading of about 40-60 bps for a few quarters until RocketBees and Qwik networks mature.
Asset-light delivery model: dedicated regional first-mile and mid-mile partners and dedicated last-mile partners on in-house technology.
Offline initiative (width-to-depth product assortment change) went live in Q4 FY26 and drove about 15% offline GMV growth.
demand_pricing: Diapering faces irrational price competition from quick-commerce and horizontal platforms (listed and unlisted); management expects this to last 4-6 quarters.
Q4 online GMV grew about 10.5%, and online growth held at about 11-12% across all four quarters of FY26. Offline GMV grew about 15% in Q4.
Annual unique transacting customers in India multi-channel: 11 million.
India multi-channel Q4 orders +10% and GMV +12%; AOV in International is about 4x India's.
Management says the Middle East has seen some moderation in consumer sentiment and import complexities, but it is 'beyond anyone's control'.
Ages 6-12 is the fastest-growing age cohort in India multi-channel.

qa_highlights.question: What share of orders now goes through FirstCry's own delivery network, and what is the logistics cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Share rose from about 28% at end Q3 to over 40% at end March 2026, with a target of 45-50% by mid-year. Logistics cost is front-loaded by about 40-60 bps for a few quarters until networks mature.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company pause COCO store openings in FY26, and what is the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Openings were paused for capital efficiency given macro conditions. Management plans about 100 stores in FY27 across COCO and FOFO formats, citing the best offline growth in seven quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How is the gross margin pressure in diapering split between competition and input inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: The 140 bps Q3 competitive hit has continued into Q4. The remaining manufacturing-related hit from rupee depreciation and crude-linked inputs is transitory and expected to be recovered from Q2 FY27 as prices are passed through.

qa_highlights.question: Is the online growth slowdown structural, given offline grew faster than the 11% overall?
qa_highlights.answer: Online GMV grew about 10.5% in Q4 and 11-12% through FY26. Management expects RocketBees and Qwik to lift online growth in FY27, with results lagging. Product mix between online and offline has not changed.

qa_highlights.question: Can India multi-channel EBITDA grow double digits in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, citing recovery of the manufacturing hit by Q2 (three quarters of benefit), continued margin expansion in the non-diaper categories, and operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Middle East situation affecting international revenue and break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer sentiment has moderated and import complexities have emerged. Management sees this as an opportunity to optimise discounting and marketing and to improve home-brand mix, and says the focus remains sustainable growth over top-line chasing.

risks_watch: Diaper price war from quick-commerce and horizontal platforms could keep gross margins under pressure beyond the 4-6 quarter window management has given.
Management has tied the FY27 recovery to a Q2 pass-through of manufacturing costs, with rupee depreciation and crude prices as the swing factors.
Middle East consumer sentiment and import complexities could slow International, where revenue growth was about 9-10%.
Online growth has run at about 10-12% and needs to accelerate in FY27 for the stated guidance to hold.
GlobalBees brand rationalisation is due to finish by end Q1 FY27; the consolidated growth figure will lag until then.
Management declined to quantify AI-driven savings, saying the number will come in later quarterly updates. It also said there have been no buyback or acquisition discussions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the India multi-channel recovery and the FY27 growth outlook, backed by the offline and delivery-network metrics. Cautious and somewhat deflecting on diaper margins, the Middle East, and quantifying AI benefits, which management said would come in later updates.
key_quotes: We are happy to state that we continue to remain PAT and cash flow positive for an India multi-channel business for the entire FY26.
So, from Q2 onwards, the gross margin loss because of crude-linked raw metal prices and rupee depreciation should be covered.
We are already crossing 20% of our overall online orders under our Qwik initiative and where we are able to deliver the customer in less than 3 hours.
It's not small. It's going to be meaningful.

adds.what: ~100 company-owned and FOFO stores planned in FY27 (after pausing COCO openings in FY26; 10 COCO stores added in FY26)
RocketBees own-network delivery coverage to cross 50 cities (62 cities at Q4 FY26)
Qwik quick-delivery pilot in 5 cities (began 1 Dec 2025), expected to reach ~10% of B2C online shipments over FY27

growth.why: Management guides FY27 India multi-channel GMV and revenue growth to be 'much superior' to FY26's ~11% without a numeric target, backed partly by ~100 planned store openings, RocketBees coverage expansion to 62 cities, and Qwik rollout, while diapering price pressure and gross margin recovery (4-6 quarters) remain headwinds.
